title: OpenTWBench (Open Taiwan Benchmark): Taiwan-Domain Knowledge Evaluation for Large Language Models, and How the Measurement Apparatus Shapes the Score
abstract: arXiv:2610.19848v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: We present OpenTWBench, an open evaluation suite for Taiwan-domain knowledge in large language models, built around two benchmarks. tw-exam-bench contains 255,854 four-option questions across 148 academic subjects, from fifteen years of Taiwan's national examinations published as open data by the Ministry of Examination; answer keys agree across 31,312 duplicated question groups at 99.91%, with all 27 disagreements accounted for. A reviewed second pass withdrew 2,180 items whose stems depend on a figure the text does not carry; all scores use the remaining 253,674. tw-formosa-bench contains 1,696 difficulty-curated questions about everyday and contemporary Taiwan - the Taiwan that licensing examinations never ask about - generated from a community-curated corpus under a discipline in which no model writes a ground truth, and curated against a frozen seven-model pool so that the pool scored at the passing margin (46.9-74.6%, median ~54%);

translated_title: OpenTWBench（开放台湾基准）：面向大型语言模型的台湾领域知识评测，以及测量装置如何塑造分数
translated_abstract: 我们提出 OpenTWBench，这是一个用于评测大型语言模型台湾领域知识的开放式评测套件，由两个基准构成。tw-exam-bench 包含 255,854 道四选项题目，涵盖 148 个学科，源自台湾考选部以开放数据形式发布的十五年国家考试题目；在 31,312 组重复题目中，标准答案的一致率达 99.91%，且全部 27 处不一致均已得到核查说明。经过审阅的第二轮处理剔除了 2,180 道题干依赖于文本未附图表的题目；所有分数均基于剩余的 253,674 道题计算。tw-formosa-bench 包含 1,696 道经难度筛选的、关于台湾日常生活与当代台湾的题目——即执照考试从不涉及的台湾面向——这些题目从社区策展的语料库中生成，遵循“没有任何模型撰写标准答案”的纪律，并以一个冻结的七模型池作为筛选基准，使该模型池的得分落在及格边缘（46.9-74.6%，中位数约 54%）；
tldr: 该论文提出开放式台湾领域知识评测套件 OpenTWBench，包含基于台湾十五年国家考试、共 25 万余道题的 tw-exam-bench，以及关于当代台湾生活的 1,696 道难度校准题的 tw-formosa-bench，并强调数据清洗与难度校准等测量装置设计对模型评测分数的塑造作用。
en_tdlr: OpenTWBench is an open evaluation suite for Taiwan-domain knowledge in LLMs, comprising tw-exam-bench (253,674 four-option questions from 15 years of Taiwan's national examinations across 148 subjects after rigorous data cleaning) and tw-formosa-bench (1,696 difficulty-curated questions on everyday and contemporary Taiwan), demonstrating how the measurement apparatus shapes evaluation scores.
